query: For high-entropy alloys intended for harsh corrosive mechanical environments, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion, and why? Propose a controlled comparison that would test the hypothesis, predict how combined degradation and its wear and corrosion components would differ from a matched baseline, define where the prediction should hold or fail, identify supporting prior evidence, and state an observation that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: For high-entropy alloys in corrosive sliding environments, resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion is governed primarily by the mechanical integrity and repassivation kinetics of the nanometer-scale passive film relative to the contact-driven depassivation rate. If the alloy’s chemical complexity stabilizes a tougher, better-adhered, and faster-reforming Cr-rich passive film, then bare-metal exposure time under sliding is minimized, dissolution spikes are suppressed, and third-body abrasion is reduced, yielding lower combined tribocorrosion loss.
generation.material_initial_state: Two single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys processed to matched hardness and grain size. Alloy H (high-film-integrity) is formulated to form a robust Cr/Mo-rich passive film; Alloy L (low-film-integrity) is formulated with reduced passive-film-forming content to yield a less protective oxide. Bulk hardness, grain size, and counterface are controlled to be comparable.
generation.intervention: Increase passive-film-forming element content (e.g., higher Cr and Mo) and/or induce short-range order that improves film adherence in Alloy H, while holding bulk hardness and grain size similar to Alloy L.
generation.conditions: Reciprocating sliding against an inert ceramic counterbody (e.g., alumina) in aerated chloride solution (e.g., 3.5 wt% NaCl), room temperature, fixed normal load and stroke, open-circuit potential with intermittent potentiostatic holds to probe repassivation. Identical test parameters for both alloys.
generation.structural_mediator: A chemically complex, Cr-rich passive film with higher fracture toughness and adhesion to the substrate, and faster repassivation kinetics; these are mediated by local lattice distortion and short-range order in the HEA that hinder cation diffusion and stabilize the film.
generation.mechanism: The net tribocorrosion rate is set by competition between mechanical film removal (shear-induced cracking/delamination) and electrochemical film reformation. A tougher, adherent film that repassivates rapidly reduces the duration and area of bare-metal exposure, lowering dissolution current transients and maintaining a low-shear interface that limits debris generation and abrasive wear. Thus both corrosion and wear components, and their synergy, decrease when the film survives or reforms faster than it is removed.
generation.predicted_outcome: Under identical conditions, Alloy H will show: (a) lower total material loss from tribocorrosion than Alloy L (direction: decrease; magnitude likely on the order of tens of percent, but exact value is uncertain), (b) smaller and less frequent electrochemical current spikes during sliding (direction: decrease), (c) faster recovery of open-circuit potential between passes (direction: decrease in recovery time), (d) a lower wear rate measured in inert medium (direction: modest decrease due to maintained low-shear surface), and (e) a lower corrosion rate measured without sliding (direction: decrease due to more protective film). The synergy factor (excess loss beyond the sum of isolated wear and corrosion) will be smaller for Alloy H than for Alloy L.
generation.baseline: A matched HEA (Alloy L) with similar hardness and grain size but intentionally reduced passive-film stability (lower passive-forming element content), tested under the same tribocorrosion protocol.
generation.boundary: Prediction should hold in environments that support passivation (oxidizing or mildly corrosive solutions, moderate chloride with sufficient oxygen) and at contact stresses where the film can survive or repassivate between passes. It may fail in non-passivating media (strongly reducing acids), very low oxygen/high chloride conditions that prevent film formation, temperatures that alter film chemistry substantially, or under extreme loads/speeds that continuously strip any film regardless of its toughness.
generation.uncertainty: No quantitative prior data are supplied here; effect sizes are approximate and mechanism could be influenced by coupled variables (e.g., stacking-fault energy, work-hardening, debris compaction) that are not fully isolated. The relative contributions of composition versus short-range order to film toughness may differ across HEA chemistries.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate Alloy H and Alloy L with matched hardness and grain size. Verify film integrity differences by nano-scratch of the oxide, adhesion tests, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS); quantify repassivation kinetics via open-circuit potential (OCP) recovery and current transients after controlled depassivation. Perform identical reciprocating tribocorrosion tests in aerated NaCl, measure total material loss, and partition wear versus corrosion using separate tests: (i) mechanical wear in inert medium (e.g., deoxygenated, non-corrosive solution) and (ii) static corrosion without sliding. Characterize wear tracks (profilometry, SEM/FIB), friction, and film chemistry (XPS).
measurements: Total mass or volume loss under tribocorrosion
Nano-scratch or nanoindentation-derived film fracture/adhesion metrics
Wear rate in inert medium without corrosion
Surface chemistry of the passive film (XPS/ToF-SIMS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If Alloy H is experimentally confirmed to have higher passive-film integrity (higher EIS resistance, stronger adhesion/toughness) and faster repassivation, yet its total tribocorrosion loss is equal to or greater than Alloy L under identical conditions, or if total tribocorrosion loss does not decrease when film integrity and repassivation are improved while bulk hardness and microstructure are held constant, then the hypothesis is falsified.
